# Pinned capture fork

Upstream: https://github.com/sskodje/ScreenRecorderLib/tree/v7.0.1

Commit: `646383234187efd3854e6b1069612b80c3ab9981` (MIT; retain upstream `LICENSE`).

The capture-exclusion extension is isolated in `ScreenRecorderLibNative/CaptureExclusion.{h,cpp}`. Small call-site changes pass a display source's HWND list, apply it before `StartCapture`, and discard frames until their `ConfigurationIteration` includes that list. `Recorder.IsSessionWindowExclusionSupported()` exposes a metadata preflight, while session creation also queries the real COM interface. The audio engine and original frame timestamps are unchanged.

`ScreenRecorderLibNative/EncoderTuning.{h,cpp}` separately configures the selected software video encoder before `BeginWriting`. It reads and logs actual CodecAPI values, requests quality/speed 25 and two video encoder workers, and verifies each change. Diagnostic overrides support baseline/auto/4/2 comparisons without affecting audio threads, mouse threads, sample timing, or sink-writer backpressure. Unsupported tuning keeps the existing codec settings. Hardware-requested sessions bypass this module. See [encoder tuning and validation](ENCODER-TUNING.md).

`ScreenRecorderLibNative/VideoSampleDiagnostics.{h,cpp}` and `VideoSampleMetrics.h` add optional observation around the unchanged video WriteSample calls. `FRAMEFLOW_CAPTURE_SAMPLE_DIAGNOSTICS=1` collects fixed-size input timing/wait statistics and first/last samples, then reports once after finalization. Default encoding, sample properties, queue/flush behavior and audio remain unchanged. See [sample diagnostics](../VIDEO-SAMPLE-DIAGNOSTICS.md).

`EncodedSampleTiming`, `EncodedTimingLedger` and the thin `EncodedTimingSink`/`EncodedTimingStream` wrappers restore each confirmed hardware encoder output's exact source duration before fragmented MP4 muxing. This safeguard is enabled inside the hardware fragmented path; `FRAMEFLOW_CAPTURE_ENCODED_TIMING=0` explicitly disables it for diagnostics. The application now prefers hardware with startup software fallback. Its 512-entry map stores metadata only. Confirmed hardware with normal writer backpressure uses non-discarding periodic metadata health checks; explicit `FRAMEFLOW_CAPTURE_STALE_MAINTENANCE=flush` and other paths retain the original flush. Original writer/stream flushes discard matching metadata. Maintenance and finalization failures, including the asynchronous writer callback, propagate without being overwritten. `MediaClockOrigin.h` separately exposes read-only native presentation-clock/QPC correlation. See [exact encoded duration design and tests](../ENCODED-SAMPLE-TIMING.md).

`frameflow-live-preview.patch` adds `RecorderMode.Preview` to the public managed enum and its native counterpart. The existing capture pipeline already gates media-sink initialization and writes on `Video`; preview mode retains those guards and uses the same frame interval as video while only delivering bitmap callbacks. `LiveCaptureSession` uses it with video-frame preview enabled and audio disabled, without a sink writer, encoded media or recording project. In 0.9.14, the existing preview callbacks were extracted into `RecordingManagerPreview.cpp`. Preview startup waits for the first real source frame before publishing callbacks, so an uninitialized fixed-framerate placeholder cannot acknowledge successful capture; native startup errors reach the live-update rollback path. The mode is additive and leaves the existing video/slideshow/screenshot enum values and recording behavior intact. It does not provide virtual-camera registration: that independent Windows SDK implementation lives in [virtual-camera](../virtual-camera/README.md). See live mode（内部历史资料未纳入本快照）.
The Windows SDK 26100 already projects `Windows.UI.WindowId`; the two newer capture interfaces are declared locally with Microsoft's published ABI. HWNDs are converted by `GetWindowIdFromWindow` from the system `Windows.UI.dll`. The input is a real `IIterable<WindowId>`, not an iterable of integers. This implementation never calls `SetWindowDisplayAffinity` or substitutes a pixel mask when the API is unavailable.

The sixth patch, `frameflow-recording-exclusions.patch`, adds `Recorder.UpdateSessionWindowExclusions(sourceId, HWNDs)` to the running display recorder. `WindowExclusionState` passes immutable, numbered requests from the command thread to the existing WGC capture thread; only that thread calls the capture session. The command waits for a frame whose `ConfigurationIteration` satisfies the requested filter, with a bounded timeout. Empty lists explicitly clear third-party exclusions. The helper merges trusted own-window handles on every change and restores the last successful list on failure. No recorder, audio track, writer or recording clock is restarted. Refresh re-enumerates newly created/revealed windows. See recording exclusions（内部历史资料未纳入本快照）.

Gradual extraction before this feature moved source conversion into `Recorder.Sources.cpp`, the source data model into `RecordingSourceBase.h`, and frame retrieval into `WindowsGraphicsCapture.Frames.cpp`. The remaining large upstream files retain their other responsibilities; later refactors should continue one module at a time. Header-defined bridge helpers are inline so the additional translation units do not duplicate symbols.

Official API references:

- [SetWindowExclusionList](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.idisplaygraphicscapturesession.setwindowexclusionlist?view=winrt-28000)
- [Microsoft's capture interface ABI](https://github.com/microsoft/windows-rs/blob/master/crates/libs/windows/src/Windows/Graphics/Capture/mod.rs)
- [GetWindowIdFromWindow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/windows.ui.interop/nf-windows-ui-interop-getwindowidfromwindow)

Run `native/scripts/fetch-recorder-fork.ps1` to fetch the exact commit and apply `frameflow-exclusion.patch`, `frameflow-encoder-tuning.patch`, `frameflow-sample-diagnostics.patch`, then `frameflow-encoded-timing.patch`, `frameflow-live-preview.patch` and `frameflow-recording-exclusions.patch`, followed by `python native/tools/bootstrap_toolchain.py` and `native/scripts/build-recorder-fork.ps1`. The compiler/SDK are extracted only into `.native-build-tools` and are not installed globally. Official download receipts and component licenses are retained there; see `native/tools/README.md`. The build writes `native/vendor/artifacts/ScreenRecorderLib.dll`, which is the helper's explicit assembly reference. Every build compiles all native sources, avoiding stale objects after header changes; `-ReuseNativeObjects` is rejected because this custom build has no header dependency graph.

The upstream project contains existing large files. New exclusion logic remains in its own small module, while the managed bridge/source definitions receive only the required property and conversion calls.

## Repository contents and binary provenance

Commit `artifacts/ScreenRecorderLib.dll`, all six patches, the fetch/build scripts, `native/tools/components.lock.json`, and their documentation. The DLL is the explicit assembly reference used by `FrameFlow.Capture.csproj`. A normal fresh-clone helper build needs this DLL, the .NET 8 SDK, and NuGet restore for NAudio.Wasapi 2.3.0; rebuilding the C++ fork is a separate step.

The current binary (1,190,400 bytes) was rebuilt from all 38 native translation units and the managed C++/CLI bridge (including source conversion in its own translation unit) on 2026-10-06; the subsequent native helper build also passed. Sample observations remain off by default. Exact encoded duration repair is enabled inside the hardware fragmented path, with an explicit diagnostic off switch. Confirmed hardware with normal throttling now replaces destructive periodic flushing with bounded metadata health checks by default, after controlled static/animated three-minute and crash-recovery comparisons passed. Software and disabled timing/throttling keep the original policy; explicit `FRAMEFLOW_CAPTURE_STALE_MAINTENANCE=flush` restores it for hardware diagnostics. Finalization preserves asynchronous failures, failed startup releases its writer and sink, and the additive live-preview mode avoids media encoding and file output, and read-only APIs expose the running native clock's QPC origin and current frame's media endpoint:

The upstream commit remains `646383234187efd3854e6b1069612b80c3ab9981`. A fresh temporary Git index at that commit, followed by all six patches in order, matches all current source files after line-ending normalization. Current six-patch replay evidence is in `native/scripts/fetch-recorder-fork.ps1 (verified 6/6 on 2026-10-06)`; the earlier four-patch evidence is in `output/encoded-sample-timing/patch-replay.txt`; the earlier two-patch binary evidence remains in `output/encoder-capability-probe/replay.txt`. The fetch script recognizes complete ordered patch prefixes in a temporary index, preserves the real index and rejects unexpected local source changes. These hashes identify the artifact and source inputs; a new compiler run is not claimed to produce a byte-identical DLL. Update the binary and patch hashes when replacing them.

The earlier three-patch observation binary was 1,155,072 bytes, SHA-256 `7345dbc8ff5bdbe5ba61ad15d1b36130a546a88146c0a7e87044f201385ddd9a`. Its hardware fragmented/standard MP4 comparisons predate the optional duration repair. The previous 0.8.1 two-patch binary was 1,149,440 bytes with SHA-256 `cf450f95df5f51069d45bc9f021bbaf3a823325a957862b7e7cd52c9b352b6ab`; those older reports contain no input sample observations.

Ignore the entire `native/vendor/ScreenRecorderLib/` checkout, including its nested `.git`; `fetch-recorder-fork.ps1` recreates it at the pinned upstream revision and applies the committed patch. Do not add the nested repository as a gitlink: its local fork changes would be omitted. Do not merely remove its `.git` and commit the extracted source without revising the fetch workflow, because that script validates the upstream Git HEAD.

Only `ScreenRecorderLib.dll` is retained under `artifacts/`. The static `.lib`, `obj/`, generated shader headers, and build logs are rebuildable outputs. The `.native-build-tools/` compiler/SDK cache, helper/test `bin/` and `obj/`, and publish/test-publish directories are also generated and do not belong in source control.

Retain `native/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` in source and distribution. It includes the ScreenRecorderLib, NAudio, compiled fifo_map header, and C++/WinRT MIT notices; the native helper project copies it to publish output. Compiler and SDK download receipts and package licenses remain in the local tool cache, whose binaries are not distributed with the application.
